title: Server actions in me/actions.ts perform privileged writes without authorization
description:
src/app/me/actions.ts starts with 'use server', so every export is a Next.js Server Action — a public HTTP endpoint. Confirmed against .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json: all 21 registered action ids carry the action-browser layer, and 12 are reachable from the webhook route's module graph.

processWebhookEvent and storeWebhookEvent are among them. They accept a caller-supplied event argument, use createAdminClient (service role, bypasses RLS), write player_customer.membership_status, and invoke handle_upgrade_team_invites — with no session or authorization check. Sibling actions in the same file (createTeam) do call getSession and throw Unauthorized, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate.

Next.js guidance is explicit that Server Actions are public endpoints and must verify authorization themselves; reachability of an action id is not a security boundary.

Present in production today under the Lemon Squeezy integration — not introduced by the Polar migration.

FIX IN PROGRESS: wordle-teams-c6v moves both functions into src/lib/polar/webhook.ts, a module without the 'use server' directive, so they stop being actions at all. That closes this specific path.

STILL TO AUDIT after that: the remaining exports of me/actions.ts. getCheckoutUrl(user: User) takes a caller-supplied User rather than deriving it from the session, which is the same class of problem at lower severity.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: no export of a 'use server' module performs a privileged write without deriving identity from the session, and getCheckoutUrl derives the player from the session rather than a caller-supplied argument.
notes:
FULLY FIXED as of ymy. getCheckoutUrl now takes NO arguments and derives the player from the session via getUserFromSession, as does the new getBillingPortalUrl; both live in src/lib/polar/actions.ts. The previous getCheckoutUrl(user: User) accepted caller-supplied identity on what Next.js treats as a public HTTP endpoint.

Registered server actions across the three commits: 21 (12 reachable from the webhook route) -> 19 -> 16. The reduction comes from deleting the two webhook handlers and the duplicate getCheckoutUrl copies.

Verified: 14 assertions covering both actions rejecting unauthenticated callers WITHOUT calling Polar at all, using the session id and email rather than any argument, and — asserted directly — having an arity of zero, so no caller-supplied identity is even expressible.
close_reason: Both webhook handlers and both billing actions no longer accept caller-supplied identity; action count 21 -> 16

title: Polar P2e: DB migration - auth hook, drop columns, webhook idempotency
description:
One migration file. THE INTERNAL ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING:

  1. create or replace public.custom_access_token_hook FIRST, dropping the user_customer_id and user_member_variant claims
  2. THEN alter table public.player_customer drop column customer_id, drop column membership_variant
  3. create unique index webhook_events_webhook_id_key on public.webhook_events (webhook_id)

If the columns are dropped while the old hook still selects them, custom_access_token_hook throws and EVERY LOGIN BREAKS. This project already has a login-lockout incident (wordle-teams-jvt) in its history. Base the new hook on supabase/migrations/20240325200437_add_customerid_back_into_auth_hook.sql, keeping user_member_status / user_first_name / user_last_name and removing the other two.

Then regenerate src/lib/database.types.ts via npm run gen-types.

P0 because this is the single riskiest step in the migration.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: migration applies cleanly on dev, login still works on dev afterward, player_customer has only (id, player_id, membership_status), and a duplicate webhook_id insert is rejected by the unique index.
notes:
Done. supabase/migrations/20260731120000_polar_migration_drop_lemonsqueezy_columns.sql, verified against a real local Postgres (not just written).

FOUND DURING VERIFICATION — webhook_id was uuid, not text. The spec and this issue both claimed it was already text and needed no change. It was uuid, because Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it. Standard Webhooks explicitly does NOT require a UUID — the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W, which a uuid cast rejects. Left alone, the first non-UUID id from Polar would throw on insert, return 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event that could never be stored. The migration now converts the column to text. Spec corrected; c6v updated.

SCOPE MOVED: gen-types moved to ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts here would break typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, which is ymy's type-ripple scope. This migration touches no TypeScript, so the repo stays green.

OTHER DECISIONS: unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null) so legacy null rows stay exempt. Dedupe before indexing orders by processed desc, id asc, so a retry set containing one processed and one failed row keeps the processed one. 'immutable' volatility on the hook was deliberately preserved to keep this migration to one concern — filed separately as wordle-teams-wau.

VERIFIED LOCALLY (supabase db reset, then psql): player_customer is exactly (id, player_id, membership_status); both columns gone; no remaining function or RLS policy references either; the hook INVOKES without throwing for both an unknown user and a real pro player, returning the three expected claims — this is the login-safety proof; webhook_id is text; the partial unique index exists; a non-UUID Standard Webhooks id inserts fine; a duplicate raises a unique violation; two null webhook_ids are both allowed; member_status enum unchanged.
close_reason: Migration written and verified against a local Postgres; caught and fixed a uuid/text column bug that would have broken the webhook pipeline

title: P0: /login is completely unusable for anyone blocking lemonsqueezy.com — infinite error loop locks the page
description:
REPRODUCED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. If app.lemonsqueezy.com fails to load, the login page enters an infinite error loop, pegs the main thread, never renders, and the tab eventually crashes. Affected users cannot sign in or sign up AT ALL.

MEASURED (headless Chromium, prod https://wordleteams.com/login, fresh profile):
 - normal load: renders fine, createLemonSqueezy defined, 0 errors
 - lemon.js request aborted: 998 'createLemonSqueezy is not a function' errors within the first 500ms;
 document.body.innerText() times out after 3s (main thread locked);
 page never renders the sign-in UI; tab crashes shortly after
 - lemon.js delayed 0.5/1.5/3s: 0 errors, renders fine

So the trigger is FAILURE TO LOAD, not slowness. beforeInteractive defers hydration until the script resolves, so a slow network is safe; an aborted/blocked request is not.

THE LOOP (all four links confirmed in code):
 1. src/components/app-bar/app-bar-base.tsx:34-35 — useEffect calls window.createLemonSqueezy() unguarded, as its FIRST statement.
 2. src/app/login/layout.tsx renders <Welcome />, and src/components/welcome.tsx:21 renders <AppBar />. So AppBar lives in the LAYOUT of the /login segment.
 3. Next.js error.tsx does not catch errors thrown by the layout of its own segment, so src/app/login/error.tsx cannot catch it. There is no src/app/error.tsx. It bubbles all the way to src/app/global-error.tsx.
 4. src/app/global-error.tsx:15 renders <AppBar /> — the same component that just threw. It throws again. Loop.

SENTRY: issue 6834987895, 3380 events / 11 users, first seen 2025-08-25, still firing 2026-07-26. Sampled transactions: /login 447, /home 63, / 3, /terms 1 — never /me. ~63 events per session is the loop signature.

WHO IS BLOCKED: app.lemonsqueezy.com is a payments/tracking domain blocked by uBlock Origin + EasyPrivacy, Brave Shields, Safari content blockers, Pi-hole/NextDNS, and corporate/school DNS filtering. Note the churn data in wordle-teams-456: a large share of never-activated accounts are on school and corporate domains (multiple k12/university and enterprise domains) — exactly the networks most likely to filter that domain.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the failure is 100% client-side, so Vercel/Axiom logs show nothing — which is why the earlier log-only pass found 163 visitors reaching /login with only ~12 completing auth and zero server errors. Sentry's 11-user count is an undercount: the /monitoring tunnel drops ~11% of events (306x 400, 87x 429), and an ad-blocker that blocks lemonsqueezy will usually block the Sentry tunnel too — the users most affected are the least able to report it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Guard the call: if (typeof window.createLemonSqueezy === 'function') before invoking, and move the LemonSqueezy Setup into its own useEffect so a failure cannot block the PWA and time-zone logic that follow it in the same effect. 2) Move the <Script> out of the component into the root layout, or load it lazily only where checkout is actually used. 3) Remove <AppBar /> from src/app/global-error.tsx so the error fallback can never re-trigger the error it is displaying. 4) Add src/app/error.tsx so page-level errors stop escalating to global-error. 5) Re-run scripts/repro-login.mjs with lemon.js blocked and confirm the sign-in UI renders with 0 errors.
notes: SHIPPED TO PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. Merged dev (aeb3c00) then main (762cbda); Vercel production deploy Ready. Verified against live https://wordleteams.com/login with the regression script: lemon.js allowed PASS, lemon.js BLOCKED PASS (0 errors, page responsive, sign-in UI rendered). Was 998 errors in 500ms with an unresponsive page. Next: watch Sentry issue 6834987895 for new events — it should go quiet — then re-measure the login funnel in wordle-teams-390.
close_reason: Fixed in a5d91f1 on branch fix/login-lemonsqueezy-lockout. Verified on a local production build: with lemon.js blocked, 0 createLemonSqueezy errors and the sign-in UI renders (was 998 errors in 500ms with the page unresponsive). All 5 acceptance criteria met: guarded call driven by Script onReady, strategy corrected to afterInteractive, setup split out of the mount effect, AppBar removed from global-error.tsx, src/app/error.tsx added. Regression check at scripts/repro-login-lockout.mjs. Still needs a production deploy before the funnel can be re-measured.

title: Polar P3: verification script and dev verification
description:
No test framework exists, so this follows the established scripts/*.mjs pattern.

CREATE scripts/verify-polar-sandbox.mjs - creates a checkout and a portal session by external_customer_id, asserts both return usable URLs.

VERIFY ON DEV: (1) Exercise mapEventToTransition over every Polar event name - pure, so no network or DB needed. (2) Complete a sandbox checkout with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 against dev; assert the webhook_events row, the player_customer transition, and the RPC's effect on teams. (3) LOGIN REGRESSION - highest stakes, because of the auth hook rewrite. Per the standing note, dev.wordleteams.com is behind Vercel SSO so curl cannot reach it; this must go through supabase-js against dev Supabase the way scripts/validate-invite-dev.mjs already does. (4) Confirm subscription.canceled alone does NOT downgrade - the single most important behavioral difference from the LS integration.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: all four checks pass on dev against Polar sandbox, with the canceled-does-not-downgrade case explicitly demonstrated.
notes:
FROM c6v — additional coverage this issue must provide, beyond what was already listed:

3. THE FULL PAYLOAD PATH THROUGH validateEvent. Polar's subscription payload schema requires dozens of fields (recurring_interval among them), so a hand-built fixture would drift from the real schema and give false confidence. It was deliberately NOT faked. Consequence: nothing yet proves a REAL Polar payload parses and that event.data.customer.externalId is populated where the route reads it. A live sandbox subscription.active is the first thing that exercises this — if the external id lands somewhere else in the payload, the route will 202 every event and silently never upgrade anyone. Check for 202s in the logs, not just for absence of 500s.

4. Confirm the header is literally 'webhook-id' on real deliveries. The route 400s without it.

Already verified offline in c6v (31 assertions, no live services): every transition including canceled/past_due NOT downgrading, replay via 23505, unknown player via 23503, transient errors returning 500 so Polar retries, markProcessed failure not causing redelivery of applied work, and invalid/absent signatures being rejected 403 without ever reaching the database.

description:

No third-party payment script remains afterward, which also removes the DNS-filter failure mode app-bar-base.tsx currently carries defensive code and a comment about.

CHECKOUT CALLSITES: user-dropdown.tsx, month-dropdown/month-dropdown.tsx, teams-dropdown/teams-dropdown.tsx change from window.LemonSqueezy.Url.Open(url) to window.location.href = url. getCheckoutUrl currently exists TWICE (src/app/me/actions.ts:399 and src/components/app-bar/actions.ts:23) as near-identical duplicates imported from two different modules by those three callsites - consolidate to one server action.

That retry is new - webhook delivery races the browser redirect and today that race is silent.

PORTAL: sendToBillingPortal drops its user.customerId guard and calls a server action deriving the player from the session. Show the menu item only when memberStatus is pro/cancelled/expired, and toast gracefully on the 404 that occurs when a user who never checked out has no Polar customer.

Done. Lemon Squeezy is entirely gone: src/lib/lemonsqueezy/, shims.d.ts, src/types/global.d.ts, the lemon.js <Script> and its Checkout.Success handler, and the @lemonsqueezy/lemonsqueezy.js dependency. 'grep -ri lemon' over the repo now returns nothing outside git history.

gen-types: ran it, then DISCARDED most of the output. The regeneration produced 234 changed lines, of which only 6 were ours (player_customer losing customer_id and membership_variant). The other 228 were storage-schema churn from local Postgres image drift — types that may not even match production, and exactly the problem commit e2d9ee0 complains about. Applied the 6-line change surgically instead. Anyone re-running gen-types should expect the same and do the same.

Checkout UX: three callsites now do window.location.href instead of the overlay. Billing menu gating changed from proMember to pro/cancelled/expired, so a lapsed subscriber can still reach the portal, and sees Upgrade alongside it.

CheckoutReturn is mounted on BOTH /me return paths, including the no-teams Intro branch — someone who upgrades before creating a team lands there, and without it a slow webhook would leave them showing as free with nothing to trigger a refresh.

Fixed while here: a narrowing bug in getBillingPortalUrl. 'if (result.url)' does not narrow the union because the success variant types url as string and '' is falsy, which made the no-customer branch unreachable. Now compares against null.

Verified: tsc clean, build exits 0, no new lint warnings (the two app-bar-base/user-dialog exhaustive-deps warnings are pre-existing and the diff there is pure deletion), and 82 assertions across four suites all pass.

title: Polar P2d: rewrite webhook route for Polar
description:
Rewrite src/app/api/webhook/route.ts. Path stays /api/webhook (one provider, still accurate).

FLOW: (1) validateEvent(rawBody, headers, secret) from @polar-sh/sdk/webhooks; on WebhookVerificationError return 403. (2) playerId = event.data.customer.external_id. (3) If missing or not a UUID, log and return 202 NOT 500 - webhook_events.player_id is NOT NULL with an FK to players, so a foreign event would fail the insert and make Polar retry forever on something that can never succeed. (4) webhookId from the 'webhook-id' HEADER - Polar follows Standard Webhooks, so unlike LS's meta.webhook_id it is not in the body. Column is already text, no type change. (5) Store event; on unique-index conflict it is an already-handled retry, return 200. (6) Apply transition from P2b, run the RPC, mark processed.

Also delete src/lib/typeguards.ts outright - validateEvent returns discriminated typed events, so webhookHasMeta/webhookHasData have nothing left to guard. Update processWebhookEvent/storeWebhookEvent in src/app/me/actions.ts:292-397 accordingly, including deleting the per-webhook getFreeVariantId() API call.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a valid sandbox event updates player_customer and runs the right RPC; an invalid signature returns 403; a replayed webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing; an event with an unknown external_id returns 202.
notes:
CORRECTION from j8c: the issue description says webhook_id is 'already text, no type change'. That was WRONG — the column was uuid (Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one, and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it). Migration 20260731120000 now converts it to text, verified locally. Standard Webhooks does not require UUIDs; the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Do NOT assume the header value parses as a UUID.

ALSO FROM j8c: gen-types moved OUT of j8c and into ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts breaks typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, and fixing those is ymy's type-ripple scope. j8c therefore shipped SQL only, keeping the repo green.

The unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null), so legacy rows with a null webhook_id are exempt. A duplicate non-null webhook_id raises a unique violation on insert — catch that specifically and return 200, since it means an already-handled retry.
close_reason: Webhook route rewritten for Polar; also closed the server-action escalation path, proven via the build manifest

title: Polar P2c: checkout and portal modules
description:
Create src/lib/polar/checkout.ts with createProCheckout(playerId, email, name) -> checkout URL, and src/lib/polar/portal.ts with getCustomerPortalUrl(playerId).

Checkout uses POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID directly (replacing the current listProducts + .find(p => p.attributes.name === 'Pro') name lookup, deleting an API round-trip per checkout and a fragile string match). Sets external_customer_id = playerId, prefills customer email/name, and sets success_url to /me?checkout=success on the environment-appropriate origin (the existing url ternary in src/lib/lemonsqueezy/index.ts:14-20 has the right shape).

Portal creates a customer session via external_customer_id rather than a stored Polar customer UUID - this is what lets player_customer.customer_id be dropped entirely. Portal URLs are short-lived, so always generate fresh at click time, never store.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: both functions return usable URLs against Polar sandbox, and the portal path never reads a customer id from the database.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/checkout.ts (createProCheckout) and src/lib/polar/portal.ts (getCustomerPortalUrl). client.ts gained proProductIds() returning [annual, monthly] and appOrigin(); POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID replaced by the monthly/annual pair.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: portal.ts first matched a missing customer with 'error instanceof ResourceNotFound'. That check can NEVER match. The SDK only raises its typed error classes for responses declared in the OpenAPI spec, and customerSessions.create does not declare a 404 — it throws the generic SDKError. Probing the SDK with a stubbed 404 confirmed: 'THREW SDKError', not ResourceNotFound. Shipped as written, every player who had never checked out would have been told to try again later, forever, for a condition retrying can never fix. Now matched on 'error instanceof PolarError && error.statusCode === 404'. PolarError is the base of both classes and carries statusCode, so it holds whichever a future SDK version throws.

getCustomerPortalUrl returns a discriminated PortalResult ({url} | {url:null,reason:'no-customer'} | {url:null,reason:'error'}) so ymy's UI can say something true instead of a generic retry message. no-customer logs at info, not error — it is an expected state, not a fault.

appOrigin() follows the VERCEL_URL convention from src/lib/auth-urls.ts rather than the hardcoded ENVIRONMENT ternary the Lemon Squeezy module used. Noted in a comment as worth consolidating with auth-urls.ts if a third caller appears.

Verified: tsc clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 22 assertions pass by intercepting fetch — asserting the exact request body Polar receives (both products, annual first, external_customer_id, no customer UUID, success_url, return_url), every failure branch, the log levels, and that neither module imports supabase. Live URL round-trip deferred to P3 (8sg), which has been updated.
close_reason: Checkout and portal modules landed; caught an unreachable error branch that would have broken the billing portal for all non-subscribers

The lazy-memoized client and the env validation pattern this issue established are unchanged.

title: Polar P2b: pure event-mapping module
description:
Create src/lib/polar/events.ts with mapEventToTransition(eventType) -> { status, rpc } | null. Pure function, no I/O, no Supabase, no network - it holds the only real logic in the integration and is the unit most worth verifying independently.

MAPPING (see epic for why cancel != revoke):
  subscription.active     -> pro,     rpc: upgrade
  subscription.uncanceled -> pro,     rpc: upgrade (no-op if already pro)
  subscription.canceled   -> null     (NO CHANGE - access paid through period end)
  subscription.past_due   -> null     (NO CHANGE - recoverable)
  subscription.revoked    -> expired, rpc: downgrade

revoked maps to 'expired' unconditionally; distinguishing 'cancelled' would cost a payload branch and nothing reads the difference - only 'pro' gates anything.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: every one of the five subscribed event names returns the mapping above, and an unknown event name returns null rather than throwing.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/events.ts exports mapEventToTransition(eventType), ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS, and the MembershipTransition / MembershipRpc types. rpc values are the literal Postgres function names (handle_upgrade_team_invites / handle_downgrade_team_removal) so P2d has no indirection to resolve.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: the first implementation used Record<string, ...>, whose lookup walks the prototype chain. mapEventToTransition('toString') returned Object.prototype.toString (a Function) and '__proto__' returned {} — both truthy, both violating the documented 'unknown yields null' contract, and both would have reached P2d as a truthy transition with an undefined status, producing a database write of undefined membership_status. Not exploitable, since event types arrive inside signature-validated Polar payloads, but the contract was wrong. Switched to a Map, which has no prototype chain. Also froze the shared GRANT/REVOKE objects: both grant events return the same object, so an unfrozen result let a caller mutating one silently corrupt the other.

CROSS-CHECK WORTH REPEATING IN P2D: the verification reads the 37 event-type string literals straight out of @polar-sh/sdk's payload .d.ts files and asserts every acknowledged name exists among them. This specifically guards the British 'subscription.cancelled' typo, which is easy to write here because the app's own member_status enum uses 'cancelled' while Polar's event is 'subscription.canceled'.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 26 assertions pass covering the five mapped events, seven unknown names, four prototype keys, the SDK cross-check, ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS contents, and the freeze behavior.
close_reason: Event mapping landed and verified; 26 assertions pass, prototype-chain bug found and fixed during verification

title: Polar P1: dashboard + Vercel env setup (owner task)
description:
Owner-executed. Full runbook: docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md. Create sandbox org at sandbox.polar.sh and production org at polar.sh (separate instances, separate tokens). Pro product in each matching current LS Pro price. Org access tokens with checkout/customer-session/customer/product permissions. Webhook endpoints in Raw format subscribed to subscription.active, .uncanceled, .canceled, .revoked, .past_due. Six Vercel env vars (POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID across Production and Preview scopes).

LEAD TIME RISK: Polar reviews orgs before enabling live payments. Submit the production org for review FIRST since it gates prod verification.

DEV WEBHOOK GOTCHA: dev.wordleteams.com is behind Vercel Deployment Protection and would silently block Polar webhooks. Sandbox webhook URL must carry the automation bypass secret as a query param: https://dev.wordleteams.com/api/webhook?x-vercel-protection-bypass=SECRET. That URL contains a secret and this repo is PUBLIC - dashboard and Vercel env only, never committed.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: both Pro products exist at matching prices, all six Vercel env vars set, both webhook endpoints registered with the five events in Raw format, and production org review submitted.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-07-31 during execution: Pro is TWO products per environment, not one. Polar has no variants — each product has a single pricing model and its billing cycle is locked at creation — so monthly and annual are separate products with separate UUIDs. That means four products total (monthly + annual, in sandbox and in production).

Env vars accordingly go from three to four: POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID is replaced by POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID and POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID, so eight values across Production and Preview scopes rather than six.

This costs no application code. A Polar checkout session accepts a products array and renders the options side by side on the hosted page, so the customer picks the interval there instead of in the app. docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md has been updated in full.

title: EPIC: Migrate billing from Lemon Squeezy to Polar.sh
description:
Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-polar-migration-design.md. Owner runbook for dashboard setup: docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md. Branch: feat/polar-migration.

WHY NOW: Polar cannot import active subscriptions from Lemon Squeezy (polar-migrate moves products/customers/discounts only). Every paying customer must re-subscribe by hand, so the cost scales with subscriber count and is at its minimum at one paying customer.

KEY DECISIONS: (1) Hard cutover, LS removed entirely in one release. (2) No Polar Free product; 'free' is a DB default, never webhook-driven. (3) external_customer_id = player_id, so Polar customer UUID is never stored, which lets player_customer.customer_id AND membership_variant both be DROPPED rather than retyped int->uuid. (4) Downgrade on subscription.revoked ONLY, never on subscription.canceled, because Polar splits cancel-scheduled from access-ended and a literal port would strip a paying customer's teams weeks early. (5) Hosted redirect checkout, no third-party script, which also removes the DNS-filter failure mode lemon.js has. (6) Customer email held until dev is verified so cutover is a deploy, not a project.

OUT OF SCOPE: polar-migrate tooling; the three Postgres RPCs (handle_upgrade_team_invites, handle_downgrade_team_removal, handle_free_team_limit) which branch on membership_status='pro' and stay untouched by design; the two untracked scripts/*-dev.mjs files in the working tree.

HIGHEST RISK: the migration must 'create or replace' custom_access_token_hook BEFORE dropping player_customer.customer_id and membership_variant, in the same file. Dropping first makes the hook throw and breaks EVERY login. This project already has a login-lockout incident in its history.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New user completes Polar checkout and lands on /me as pro without manual refresh. 2. subscription.revoked downgrades player and removes teams beyond free limit. 3. subscription.canceled alone does NOT change membership_status or remove teams. 4. Existing pro user can open Polar customer portal from user dropdown. 5. Login works after auth hook migration, verified on dev before prod. 6. No Lemon Squeezy reference remains in codebase or Vercel env vars. 7. Duplicate webhook deliveries are idempotent (repeated webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing).

title: Hydration error + streaming-reveal crash on /me in production (muted in Sentry, 9 users)
description:
Two Sentry issues on the board page that are almost certainly one root cause. Both are PRODUCTION (vercel-production, https://wordleteams.com/me), not dev:

  6804715751  'Hydration Error'                            449 events,  9 users, status IGNORED, last 2026-07-27
  7103187406  TypeError: null is not an object (b.parentNode)  312 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-12

9 users is the second-highest user count in the whole project, behind only the login lockout (wordle-teams-jvt). The sampled events are Mobile Safari / iPhone (iOS 18.7).

The b.parentNode stack is 'app:///me:2 in $RS'. $RS is React's inline streaming-reveal helper (completeBoundary), which moves content out of a hidden template div into a resolved Suspense slot. A null parentNode means the target node was already detached when the boundary resolved — the classic downstream symptom of a hydration mismatch causing React to discard and re-render server HTML. Same page, same environment, same platform as the hydration error, so treat them as one bug until proven otherwise.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED: issue 6804715751 is set to IGNORED in Sentry, so it does not appear in any 'is:unresolved' query — which is how the 2026-07-30 triage pass enumerated issues. It only surfaced when the issues endpoint was queried with an empty status filter. Muted issues need a periodic explicit sweep.

Note the sibling issue 6809975309 ('Cannot read properties of null (parentNode)', 1070 events) is NOT this bug — its events are vercel-preview / dev.wordleteams.com, i.e. dev noise. Do not spend time on it.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce on iOS Safari against production /me and identify the hydration mismatch (likely a date/locale/timezone-dependent render, a Math.random or Date.now in render, or a client-only value used during SSR — the board is date-driven, so suspect date formatting first). Fix the mismatch, then un-ignore 6804715751 in Sentry and confirm the event rate drops to zero.
notes:
DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION 2026-07-30 (main 372324f, via dev 4b7d14e). NOT YET VERIFIED — deliberately left open.

Why open: /me requires an authenticated session, so the fix could not be exercised end-to-end before shipping. Build and typecheck pass, a sweep confirms no other useState initializer touches browser-only state, DatePicker handles an undefined date, and prod sanity after deploy is clean (/me 307 -> /login, /, /login, /home, /privacy all 200, and the wordle-teams-jvt browser regression check still PASSes with lemon.js allowed and blocked).

PRE-DEPLOY SENTRY BASELINE — compare against this to decide whether the fix worked:
  6804715751  'Hydration Error'                 449 events,  9 users, last 2026-07-27T13:40:40Z
  7103187406  'null is not an object (b.parentNode)'  312 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-12T17:42:45Z

Check with: node scripts/sentry-query.mjs issue 6804715751
CLOSE ONLY IF: lastSeen on 6804715751 stays before 2026-07-30 and the event count stops climbing over several days of real traffic. 6804715751 is currently IGNORED in Sentry — un-ignore it so new events are not silently swallowed while we wait. If events DO continue, the localStorage/useState theory is wrong or incomplete and the session replays attached to the issue are the next lead.

Note the second issue (7103187406) last fired 2026-07-12, so absence of new events there is weak evidence on its own — it was already quiet.

title: Login conversion: 163 human visitors reached /login in 30d, ~7% completed auth
description:
Axiom prod funnel, 2026-06-30..2026-07-30 (30d, the full retention window):

 /login GET 163 unique non-bot IPs, 317 hits
 /login POST 4 unique IPs, 9 requests <- login/signup server action submissions
 /api/auth/callback 8 unique IPs, 14 requests (12 OAuth 'code', 1 invite token_hash, 1 provider error)

So ~163 real people reached the sign-in screen and roughly 12 completed an auth round-trip. Crucially there are ZERO server-side auth failures in the window: no 'Failed to verify OTP', no 'Failed to exchange code for session', no 'Failed to sign in', no 5xx anywhere. The auth backend works. All 6 OAuth providers were verified live against prod Supabase (google, twitter, azure, github, slack, discord) — every one 302s correctly to its provider. People are abandoning at the login screen, not hitting errors.

The email path is nearly unused: only 4 IPs ever submitted the email form in 30 days, and 12 of 14 callbacks were OAuth codes. src/app/login/page.tsx:32 shows OAuthSignin first — a 3x2 grid of six icon-only buttons whose labels exist only as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:50-67). Tooltips do not appear on tap, and the heaviest login-page traffic is iPhone (105 hits / 22 IPs). Unlabeled icons on mobile is the leading hypothesis for the abandonment, but the logs cannot prove intent — this needs instrumentation, not more log reading.
acceptance_criteria: Add client-side funnel events for login-page view, provider-button click, and callback arrival so abandonment can be attributed. Then test labeled provider buttons (visible text, not tooltip-only) against the current icon grid and measure completion rate.
notes: UPDATE 2026-07-30: root cause very likely found — see wordle-teams-jvt. /login enters an infinite error loop and never renders for anyone blocking app.lemonsqueezy.com (reproduced against prod: 998 errors in 500ms, page unresponsive). That is a hard lockout, entirely client-side, and invisible in Vercel logs — which is exactly the 163-visitors/12-conversions signature this issue describes. The unlabeled-OAuth-icons hypothesis is now SECONDARY; re-measure the funnel after jvt ships before investing in login UX work.

title: Middleware never ran in production — root-level middleware.ts is ignored when using src/
description:
CORRECTED 2026-07-30. This issue was originally filed as 'middleware runs on every request incl. static assets, causing 2.4s cold starts'. That premise was WRONG. Middleware was not running at all.

ROOT CAUSE: this project uses a src/ directory, so Next resolves middleware at src/middleware.ts. A root-level middleware.ts is silently ignored — no warning, no build error. Proof:
  - the production build emitted "middleware": {} in .next/server/middleware-manifest.json, with no middleware bundle on disk and sortedMiddleware: []
  - against live prod, a signed-out GET https://wordleteams.com/me returned 200 with no redirect (it should 307 to /login)
  - moving the file to src/middleware.ts immediately produced 'ƒ Middleware 132 kB' in the build and the correct matcher list

WHAT WAS SILENTLY BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME:
  1. Maintenance mode. Flipping maintenance_prod in Edge Config did nothing; the rewrite never executed. Never tested, because it never worked.
  2. The welcome-path redirect (signed-in user on / or /login -> /me). The comment in src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:5-7 says this is specifically what keeps an installed PWA from opening on the welcome screen — so that bug is live for PWA users.
  3. Auth cookie refresh on every request. Plausible contributor to the forced logouts in wordle-teams-io0: without middleware refreshing the session, tokens age out and users get 'Invalid Refresh Token'.

NOT a security hole: every protected page does its own server-side check (src/app/me/page.tsx:31 redirects when !hasSession), so the middleware redirect was belt-and-braces, not the only gate.

THE ORIGINAL PERFORMANCE CLAIM IS UNEXPLAINED. /home 2421ms, /privacy 2258ms, /terms 2159ms, robots.txt 911ms are real measurements, but middleware cannot be the cause. The lambda invocations on robots.txt / sitemap.xml / manifest.json are their own route handlers (src/app/robots.ts, sitemap.ts, manifest.ts). For /privacy and /terms the likely explanation is a cold Next server handling a CDN miss on a prerendered page. That needs a separate investigation — see the follow-up issue.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware executes in production: a signed-out request to /me returns 307 to /login, and toggling maintenance_prod in Edge Config actually serves the maintenance page. Marketing and legal pages and static assets produce no middleware invocation. Neither an Edge Config outage nor a Supabase outage can 500 a matched route.
notes: Fixed on branch fix/middleware-cold-starts. The move is paired with two deliberate changes: (a) the matcher is now an allowlist of /, /login, /me, /branding, /complete-profile rather than a near-catch-all, so enabling middleware does not add invocations to marketing pages; (b) both halves fail open in try/catch, because this is middleware's production debut and every page behind it self-protects. Verified locally: matched routes 307 correctly, unmatched routes untouched, zero errors.
close_reason: Shipped to production 2026-07-30 (main c36d4b1, via dev da0c11d). Verified live: signed-out GET /me, /branding, /complete-profile now 307 to /login — previously 200 with no redirect because middleware never ran. Unmatched routes (/, /login, /home, /privacy, /terms, /about, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest.json) all 200 and untouched. Login page re-verified in a real browser with lemon.js both allowed and blocked: still PASS, so no regression to wordle-teams-jvt. Maintenance mode and the PWA welcome redirect are now functional for the first time — neither has ever been exercised in prod, so watch for surprises. The original 2.2s cold-start claim was misdiagnosed and is split out to its own issue.

title: Activation funnel: 87% of prod signups never enter a single board
description:
Prod data (2026-07-30, scripts/prod-activity-report.mjs): 526 players and 171 teams exist, but only 68 players have ever written a daily_scores row with non-empty guesses. 458 accounts (87%) signed up and never entered one board.

Of the 68 who did enter, 50 are outside Christian's teams and 40 of those 50 entered only 1-2 boards ever, then stopped. Only one independent team ever showed sustained multi-user usage: team 55 (5 players, 39-92 entries each, churned 2025-05-02). Current daily volume is 3-7 entries/day, essentially all from Christian's 6 teams.

This is the same population affected by the invite->join bug (epic wordle-teams-c0v): invitees who could not join the inviter's team would appear as a player row with zero scores, which is exactly this signature. Need to determine what share of the 458 zero-score accounts are invite-flow casualties vs. ordinary signup churn before concluding the invite fix addresses it.
acceptance_criteria: Bucket the 458 zero-score players by origin (invited vs. self-signup) and by whether they ever landed in a team's player_ids. Report what share is attributable to the invite bug fixed in 15d1edb vs. other causes.

Bug 1 (gate no-op): src/app/me/utils.ts:18 'if (!hasName(supabase))' is not awaited -> always false -> getTeams returns hasName:true always -> page.tsx:32 never redirects nameless users to /complete-profile.
Bug 2 (crash): src/lib/types.ts:138-139 fromDbPlayer throws on null first/last name; getTeams includes all player_ids members incl. the profile-incomplete invitee -> client TeamsProvider crash rendering the team. Hits invitee AND teammates viewing during the window.

Evidence (dev sgrx): team 43 'Test' player_ids includes 25eeb807 (owner-alt-account@redacted.invalid) with first_name=null; invited[] empty (invite join succeeded).

Fix: (1) await/derive hasName in getTeams so incomplete-profile users route to /complete-profile; (2) filter profile-incomplete players out of each team's rendered players in getTeams (reappear after they complete profile), so teammates don't crash.
acceptance_criteria: Invitee clicking invite link is routed to complete-profile, sets name, then sees the team; a teammate viewing a team with a not-yet-completed invitee does not crash.

title: Invited teammates land on empty state and can only create a team, not join inviter's team
description:
Reported by user invitee-6@redacted.invalid: created team team 206, invited people; when invitees click the email link they can only create a new team instead of seeing team 206 and entering their Wordle board.

Invite/join path (v1 app, dev branch):
- invitePlayer (src/app/me/actions.ts): for new email -> supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email,{data:{invited:true}}) + appends email to teams.invited[].
- Invitee clicks link -> /api/auth/callback -> finishSignIn (src/lib/utils.ts) -> handleInvite gates on user.user_metadata.invited===true -> rpc handle_invited_signup(invited_email,invited_id).
- handle_invited_signup (migration 20240517174331) appends invited_id to player_ids for teams WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited), removes from invited, sets user_metadata.invited=false.

Leading hypotheses (need DB/Sentry evidence to confirm):
- B: invitee authenticated via OAuth (Google) instead of clicking the emailed invite link, so the account they use lacks invited:true metadata -> handleInvite never runs.
- E: email case/whitespace mismatch between teams.invited[] entry and auth user email -> WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited) matches nothing.
- A: invitee already had an account -> inviteUserByEmail path differs.

Next: read-only prod query of teams.invited/player_ids for team 206 + auth.users metadata/providers for invitees; check Sentry for handle_invited_signup errors.
design:
Proposed fix (route invite through the callback via token_hash path the app already supports):
1. Pass redirectTo to both inviteUserByEmail calls: `/api/auth/callback?next=/me`.
2. Update Supabase INVITE email template (prod dashboard) to: {{ .SiteURL }}/api/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=invite&next=/me (uses handleEmailSignin/verifyOtp token_hash path; no PKCE code_verifier needed).
3. Ensure prod Site URL + additional_redirect_urls include app domain and /api/auth/callback.
Regression test: e2e - invitePlayer -> GET callback token_hash&type=invite -> assert redirect /me, player_ids contains invitee, invited[] cleared, user_metadata.invited=false; unit - assert inviteUserByEmail called with redirectTo.
Data remediation (after fix): resend invite to invitee-1 (unconfirmed user) or manually attach; ask invitee-6 which other emails they invited (only 1 recorded).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed with prod evidence; invitees who click invite link land on inviter's team and can enter their board; regression test added.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via prod (dcfqzbdusxhrfgvnpwqc) read-only diagnostics 2026-07-28.

Evidence:
- Team 206 team 206: player_ids=[invitee-6 only]; invited=['invitee-1@redacted.invalid'] (still pending). Only 1 invite ever recorded despite 'people'.
- auth.users invitee-1@redacted.invalid: user_metadata.invited=true, provider=email, last_sign_in_at=NULL, email_confirmed_at=NULL -> they have NEVER completed authentication. So join RPC (handle_invited_signup) is NOT the problem; it never runs.
- invitee-6 authenticated via Google (works). Only confirmed-working auth path in prod is Google OAuth (browser PKCE w/ code_verifier cookie).

Mechanism: invitePlayer calls supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email,{data:{invited:true}}) with NO redirectTo (actions.ts:120,145). Invite link therefore redirects to project Site URL, not /api/auth/callback. Clients use @supabase/ssr default PKCE (no flowType). Invitee lands unauthenticated (default template code-exchange needs a code_verifier cookie that admin-initiated invites don't have) -> never routed through handleInvite -> no team join. Login OTP works only because it uses code-entry/verifyOtp, not the email link; invite has only the email link.
close_reason: Released to prod and verified (deploy + test ran smoothly). Invite links route through callback via token_hash template; Site URL + redirect allowlist set on prod.

title: supabase start fails locally: storage container needs pgvector >= 0.7.0, image ships 0.4.0
description:
'supabase start' pulls the whole stack, applies all migrations successfully, then tears everything down because the storage-api container fails its healthcheck:

  Migration failed. Reason: An error occurred running 'init' ... pgvector >= 0.7.0 required for halfvec storage, found 0.4.0

The storage service retries, never becomes healthy, and the CLI reports LegacyHealthCheckTimeoutError and stops every container — including postgres. Net effect: no local database, so 'npm run gen-types' and any local migration testing are blocked.

The app does not use Supabase Storage, so excluding it is harmless. Working invocation:

  supabase start -x storage-api,imgproxy,studio,edge-runtime,logflare,vector,supavisor,realtime,mailpit

Discovered while verifying the Polar migration locally (wordle-teams-j8c), where the full stack had to come up to test the auth hook rewrite.

Real fix is probably bumping the postgres image version in supabase/config.toml, or updating the CLI (2.110.0 installed, 2.111.0 available). Worth resolving because ymy needs gen-types and P3 verification wants a local DB.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a plain 'supabase start' brings the stack up healthy, or supabase/config.toml and the README document the required exclude flags so the next session does not rediscover this.

title: Unexplained ~2.2s server time on prerendered marketing pages
description:
Split out of wordle-teams-sji, whose original explanation (middleware) turned out to be wrong — middleware was never running. The measurements are still real and still unexplained.

Axiom, production, 30 days, from vercel.source == 'lambda':
  /home      168 invocations  avg 2421ms   (also served 347x as 'static')
  /privacy    59 invocations  avg 2258ms
  /terms      54 invocations  avg 2159ms
  /about      97 invocations  avg  545ms
  /me        581 requests     avg 2069ms  p95 4138ms  max 6691ms

All of /home, /privacy, /terms are marked ○ (Static) in the build output, so they should be pure CDN hits with no function involved. Something is causing a CDN miss and a cold Next server render anyway.

Contrast: / averages 142ms, because the Sentry uptime bot pings it constantly and keeps it warm. That is strong evidence the 2.2s is cold-start-dominated rather than render-dominated — at ~5 human visits a day on these routes, the function is cold essentially every time.

This is the remaining half of the original churn hypothesis: real-user p75 LCP is 3678ms and p75 FCP 3605ms, both 'poor', while p75 TTFB is only 297ms (that sample is dominated by warm repeat visits from the ~6 daily actives).
acceptance_criteria: Explain why prerendered routes invoke a function at all — check Cache-Control / CDN cache headers on /home, /privacy, /terms in production, and whether anything in the root layout or a shared component opts them into dynamic rendering. Then either get them CDN-cached or accept and document the cold-start cost. Target p75 LCP under 2500ms.
notes: Do not re-blame middleware: after the fix in wordle-teams-sji it only matches /, /login, /me, /branding, /complete-profile. Re-measure after that ships, since the numbers above were taken while middleware was not running at all — whatever causes them is still present and unrelated.

title: Axiom leftovers: forced logouts on refresh-token loss, and monthly-winners RPC failures
description:
Two production log signals from the 2026-07-30 Axiom pass that were noted in analysis but never tracked.

1. FORCED LOGOUTS. 30d production: 8x 'Error [AuthApiError]: Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found' (code refresh_token_not_found) on /me and /login, plus 3x 'failed to get session, trying session refresh' and 3x 'Session refresh error, logging out: Auth session missing!'. Each one is a user silently kicked back to sign-in. On a passwordless app that means an entire magic-link or OAuth round trip to get back in — and given only ~12 people completed auth in 30 days (wordle-teams-390), losing a returning user this way is expensive. Low absolute count, but the app has ~6 daily actives, so this is not rare per-user. Worth checking whether src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:49-51 is racing concurrent refreshes: the comment there warns that logic between createServerClient and getUser() causes exactly this symptom, and the middleware runs on nearly every request (wordle-teams-sji).

2. MONTHLY WINNERS RPC. Two single errors in 30d: 'Failed to get monthly winner' (monthly-winner-celebration.tsx:43, 2026-07-12) and 'Failed to update winners table' (board-entry/form.tsx:99, 2026-07-05). The second is the more interesting one: the update_monthly_winners RPC failure is only log.error'd, and the user still sees a success toast for their board entry while the winners table silently goes stale. Whoever entered that board has a wrong winner recorded for their team that month.

Both are low-volume, so neither is urgent — but both are silent-failure shaped, which is the category that produced wordle-teams-jvt.
acceptance_criteria: For (1): determine whether the refresh-token loss is ordinary cookie expiry or a middleware refresh race, and stop logging it as an error if it is expected. For (2): surface update_monthly_winners failures to the user or retry them, so a board entry cannot report success while leaving winners stale.
notes: Reproduce the log query with: node scripts/axiom-query.mjs "['vercel'] | where ['vercel.environment'] == 'production' and level in ('error','warn') | project _time, level, message | sort by _time desc" 30d — note Axiom retention is only 30 days (wordle-teams-g8h).
close_reason: Shipped 2026-07-31 (main b796d7d, via dev 3071b29). 5zs: handleSubmit now wrapped in try/catch with setSubmitting(false) in finally, a toast telling the user their entry is preserved, and the sheet closing only on success (it previously closed on the handled failure path too, discarding what they had typed). io0: update_monthly_winners failure now surfaces a warning toast instead of a bare success while standings go stale; getUser/getSession stop calling refreshSession() when the error is literally 'Refresh Token Not Found', which cannot succeed, and log at info instead. Investigation found the forced-logout half was not a user-facing fault: zero events in 12h, and the historical ones collapse to two real session expiries amplified into 4-6 log lines by parallel checks each retrying. Typecheck and build clean; not exercised end-to-end because board entry requires an authenticated session.

title: Service worker registration fails in production — PWA install/offline broken for some users
description:
Sentry 7481850095, production, 10 events / 2 users, first 2026-05-14, last 2026-07-27:

  TypeError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker for scope ('https://wordleteams.com/')
  with script ('https://wordleteams.com/sw.js'): An unknown error occurred when fetching the script.

Seen on both / and /home. Three further singleton issues are the same code path failing at a different point, all production:

  7630550063  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scope')    /
  7629232232  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scope')    /
  7629232309  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'waiting')  /

The 'scope' and 'waiting' reads are almost certainly unguarded access to a ServiceWorkerRegistration that is undefined precisely because registration failed — so the registration handler in src/components/service-worker-registration.tsx does not defend against its own failure path, the same shape of bug as wordle-teams-jvt.

This matters beyond the error count: the app is a PWA, app-bar-base.tsx flags has_pwa on standalone launch, and a failed registration means no install prompt and no offline support for the affected user. Low event count, but the population that hits it is invisible — a user who cannot install simply does not come back.
acceptance_criteria: Guard every access to the registration object so a failed register() cannot throw a second error. Determine why sw.js fetch fails ('unknown error' usually means a network blip, an aborted navigation, or a bad Content-Type/scope header) and confirm next-pwa is emitting sw.js with the right headers in production. Verify no new events on 7481850095 after the fix.
notes:
DEPLOYED 2026-07-31 (main 418069d, via dev 67ca3d4).

ROOT CAUSE was double registration, not an unguarded handler as originally filed. Verified in production by wrapping navigator.serviceWorker.register: it was called twice per page load — once by @serwist/window (chunk 6537, serwist injects registration by default) and once by our own component. Serwist's call has no rejection handler, which is why failures reached Sentry with mechanism onunhandledrejection despite our component passing an error handler.

FIX: register: false in the serwist config, plus our component rewritten to async/await with try/catch, logging failure as a warning. Verified on a local production build: register() called exactly once, worker reaches state 'activated' at scope /, manifest link intact, no page errors.

THREE OF THE FOUR SENTRY ISSUES WERE NOT BUGS:
  7481850095  REAL — 10 events, 2 Chrome/Windows users since 2026-05-14. This is the one the fix targets.
  7629232309  NOT REAL — breadcrumb 'Service Worker registration blocked by Playwright'; our own test run.
  7630550063  NOT REAL — stack frames in ext:core/01_core.js, a Deno runtime; a crawler.
  (the third singleton 7629232232 is the same shape as 7630550063)
All three noise issues originate in @serwist/window's register path and should stop now the duplicate registration is gone.

BASELINE for the watch — 7481850095: 10 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-27T03:19:18Z. Check with: node scripts/sentry-query.mjs issue 7481850095. Low frequency (10 events in 2.5 months) means silence proves little quickly; the stronger near-term signal is that the three noise issues stop accruing.
close_reason: Verified in production 2026-07-31 on build layout-f9f3b86a3944759c. register() now called exactly once (was twice: @serwist/window plus our component), the worker reaches state 'activated' at scope https://wordleteams.com/, manifest link intact, no page errors. Full regression sweep on the same build also clean: P0 login check PASSes with lemon.js allowed and blocked, /home /privacy /terms all x-vercel-cache HIT, /me still 307. Watch Sentry 7481850095 (baseline 10 events / 2 users / last 2026-07-27) plus the two noise issues 7629232309 and 7630550063, which originated in the serwist register path that no longer runs.

title: Board entry silently hangs if the server action rejects — no try/catch in handleSubmit
description:
src/components/action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx:66-109. handleSubmit awaits upsertBoard(formData) with no try/catch. upsertBoard itself is well guarded (src/app/me/actions.ts:191-260 catches everything and returns {success:false}), so the server path is safe — but a rejection that happens BEFORE or AROUND the action body is not:

 - Next.js rejecting the action entirely ('Failed to find Server Action', e.g. a stale tab open across a deploy — very plausible for a daily-habit app where people leave the tab open)
 - network drop mid-submit, especially on mobile
 - platform-level 500

On rejection: setSubmitting(false) at line 106 never runs, no toast fires, and document.getElementById('close-board-entry')?.click() at line 108 never runs. The form stays stuck in the animate-pulse state with a spinning button, and the entered board is lost with no error shown.

LATENT, not yet observed for a real user. The 10 'Failed to find Server Action' errors in the 30d window were all scanner probes sending Next-Action: "x" from AWS IPs (<scanner-ip>, <scanner-ip>) hitting POST /, not genuine users. Filing because the failure mode is silent and the cost is a lost board entry on an app with ~6 daily users.
acceptance_criteria: Wrap the await in try/catch: surface toast.error with a retry hint, always setSubmitting(false) in a finally block, and preserve the user's entered guesses so they can resubmit without re-typing.
notes: Same file, line 94-100: the update_monthly_winners RPC failure is only log.error'd and never surfaced. It fired once in prod on 2026-07-05 ('Failed to update winners table'). Low severity but the user sees a success toast while the winners table is stale.

Investigation found the forced-logout half was not a user-facing fault: zero events in 12h, and the historical ones collapse to two real session expiries amplified into 4-6 log lines by parallel checks each retrying. Typecheck and build clean; not exercised end-to-end because board entry requires an authenticated session.

title: Auth callback ignores provider ?error= params, shows generic /login-error
description:
src/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts:15-22 reads only 'code' and 'token_hash'. When an OAuth provider returns an error instead, neither is present, so it falls through to handleEmailSignin(null, null), logs 'Token Hash or Type were missing in the auth callback', and redirects to /login-error with no explanation.

Observed in prod 2026-07-22T19:31:43Z:
 /api/auth/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=AADSTS65004%3A+User+declined+to+consent+to+access+the+app.

That user declined Microsoft consent and got a dead-end error page instead of 'you cancelled — try another sign-in method'. On a funnel where only ~12 people completed auth in 30 days (see wordle-teams-390), losing one to an unexplained error page is material.

Also seen: a paramless GET /api/auth/callback at 2026-07-17T14:51:16.93Z, followed 1.4s later by a valid one carrying a code — likely a prefetch or double-fire. The paramless hit also lands on /login-error.

Related friction on the Microsoft button specifically: src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:36 requests scopes 'email offline_access'. offline_access asks for persistent access and is a common consent-decline trigger; it is not needed unless the app refreshes Microsoft tokens server-side.
acceptance_criteria: Parse 'error' and 'error_description' in parseRequest and branch on them: show a specific, human-readable message (declined consent vs. expired link vs. unknown) rather than routing everything to /login-error. Ignore paramless callback hits without logging them as errors. Separately, confirm whether offline_access is actually required for azure and drop it if not.

title: Invite email matching is case-sensitive — join silently fails on casing mismatch
description: handle_invited_signup uses 'WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited)' (case-sensitive) and invitePlayer stores the email exactly as the inviter typed it. If the inviter types different casing than the invitee's auth email (e.g. 'invitee-7@redacted.invalid' vs 'invitee-7@redacted.invalid'), the join never matches and the invite silently fails — a second, independent cause of the invite-not-working symptom. Seen in prod (team 181 stored 'invitee-7@...'). Fix: normalize emails to lowercase when writing teams.invited (invitePlayer) and/or make handle_invited_signup match case-insensitively (lower(invited_email) = ANY(select lower(unnest(invited)))). Add regression test.
acceptance_criteria: Invites with mixed-casing emails still join the invitee to the team.
notes: Fix in PR #153 -> dev. Code: invitePlayer lowercases/trims email + invited list on write. Data: existing teams.invited normalized to deduped-lowercase on prod (8 teams) + dev (0) — LIVE now. Migration 20260730190000 adds case-insensitive handle_invited_signup (defense-in-depth) + idempotent data normalization; untested DDL, apply dev->prod via normal migration process after review. Verified on dev: mixed-case fails to join, lowercasing joins. Code+data fix alone resolves acceptance; RPC hardening optional.

title: custom_access_token_hook is declared IMMUTABLE but reads tables
description:
public.custom_access_token_hook is declared 'immutable' while performing a SELECT against public.players and public.player_customer. Postgres defines IMMUTABLE as 'cannot modify the database and always returns the same result for the same arguments', which permits the planner to pre-evaluate or cache calls. A function that reads mutable tables should be STABLE at most.

In practice the risk is low - Supabase's auth service invokes the hook directly per token issuance rather than inside a query the planner would fold - which is presumably why it has never visibly misbehaved. But the declaration is incorrect and could produce stale membership claims.

Pre-existing since 20240313202756_custom_claims.sql and carried through every subsequent redefinition, including the Polar migration (20260731120000). That migration deliberately preserved 'immutable' rather than changing it, to keep the riskiest migration in the project scoped to exactly one concern - see wordle-teams-j8c.

Changing it is a one-word migration but alters planner behavior for the function that gates every login, so it deserves its own change with its own verification.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the volatility is either corrected to STABLE with login verified on dev and prod, or a comment in the migration documents why IMMUTABLE is deliberate.

title: public/sw.js churns on every build, dirtying the working tree
description:
public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map are tracked build artifacts regenerated by serwist on every 'pnpm build'. The only delta between builds is a rerolled Sentry debug ID inside the minified bundle, so every build leaves ~96KB of meaningless diff in the working tree that has to be reverted by hand before committing anything unrelated.

Discovered while building for the Polar migration (wordle-teams-9he), where the artifact churn had to be discarded to keep the commit readable.

Options: gitignore them and generate at build time on Vercel; or configure the Sentry plugin to emit a stable debug ID; or leave as-is and keep reverting. Low priority - it is a papercut, not a defect.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a clean 'pnpm build' either leaves the working tree clean, or the churn is documented as intentional so future sessions stop reverting it.

title: Triage 'Error: Rejected' on /home in production
description:
Sentry 6835069821, production, 30 events / 1 user, https://wordleteams.com/home, last seen 2026-07-23.

'Error: Rejected' with no further detail is typically an unhandled promise rejection that Sentry could not resolve to a useful message — often a fetch abort, a cancelled navigation, or a rejected dynamic import. 30 events from a single user suggests a loop or a repeated retry rather than a broad problem.

Low priority on its own, but it is the last unexplained production Sentry issue and 30 events from one person on the marketing landing page is odd enough to be worth ten minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Identify the rejecting promise (check the attached session replay and breadcrumbs) and either fix it or add a proper catch so it reports with a usable message. If it is benign, resolve or ignore it in Sentry with a note explaining why.

title: /maintenance is listed in sitemap.xml — crawlers and searchers land on a maintenance page
description:
src/app/sitemap.ts includes /maintenance. In 30d prod, 16 unique IPs hit /maintenance — mostly crawlers (AhrefsBot, SeznamBot, PetalBot with referer https://wordleteams.com/sitemap.xml, Applebot, SERankingBacklinksBot) but also 3 real browsers (<redacted-ip> Safari 18.1, <redacted-ip> Chrome 129/Windows) with no referer, consistent with arriving from search results.

Maintenance mode itself was NOT on during the window — middleware.ts:6-10 only rewrites to /maintenance when the Edge Config flag maintenance_prod is true, and total traffic was normal. The page is simply publicly indexable because the sitemap advertises it. A prospective user finding 'Wordle Teams' via search and landing on a maintenance notice is a silent, permanent loss.
acceptance_criteria: Remove /maintenance from src/app/sitemap.ts and add noindex to the page. Confirm no non-bot traffic reaches /maintenance while the maintenance flag is off.
